claim: App-managed relay rooms can use separate digest-stored bearer members with protocol-enforced viewer/editor/admin document permissions and host-local revocation while unregistered rooms remain explicit legacy read/edit bearer rooms; this is authorization, not authenticated human identity.
commands: node ../scripts/run-with-heartbeat.mjs --timeout-seconds 120 --heartbeat-seconds 30 -- npm exec -- vitest run src/components/CollaborationRelaySettings.ui.test.tsx src/migrations.test.ts src/workspace/WorkspaceView.ui.test.ts src/workspace/websocketProjectInvite.test.ts src/workspace/websocketProjectProvider.test.ts src/workspace/websocketProjectStore.test.ts src/workspace/websocketProjectProductFlow.integration.test.ts
proved: Every managed member receives a random member ID and 256-bit capability; the strict bounded registry stores only the capability's SHA-256 digest.
Room creation, issuance, and revocation use exact registry revisions, retain one active admin, durably replace state, and restart the owned relay so current connections must reauthenticate.
The exact relay denies missing, incorrect, and revoked credentials before sending a protected room frame.
Admin and editor Yjs document updates converge and survive process restart.
A viewer receives retained document state and ephemeral awareness, while sync step-two/document-update frames close the connection before broadcast or persistence.
The managed-v2 invitation keeps member credentials separate from endpoint/room validation and the real WebsocketProjectProvider presents them through y-websocket query parameters.
A room absent from the membership registry remains compatible with the legacy-v1 room-bearer product flow.
The host UI issues one role-specific invitation per member, lists no token/digest, and exposes local issue/revoke controls only when this installation operates the room.
notProved: Authenticated human identity, organizational enrollment, or binding a signed installation fingerprint to a relay member capability/role.
Remote membership administration: admin credentials can write documents but only the relay-host installation can issue or revoke members.
Resistance after an authorized collaborator copies a bearer invitation or capability; capability recovery/rotation and invite-expiry UX remain open.
Global read-only UI for viewers: relay writes are rejected, but a viewer can create local-only edits that do not synchronize.
Research-update encryption at rest, independent backup/restore, log compaction/export, public TLS/WSS termination, or third-party relay authorization behavior.
Hostile-frame fuzzing, five-client soak, physical packaged two-install operation, cross-platform packet capture, or signed updater artifact inclusion.
